    </ix:exclude> <ix:exclude>&#160;</ix:exclude> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Revenue from the sale of products is generally recognized at a point in time when control of the goods is transferred. Certain sales contracts include services to install and commission or customize the product&#160;for customers. Revenues from these services are categorized as product&#160;revenue and recognized either over time as the services are being performed, or at a point in time, depending on the nature of the services and whether the criteria for recording revenue over time are met in accordance with ASC <em style="font: inherit;">606.</em></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 1pt;text-indent:36pt;">Revenue from development arrangements is either recognized at a point in time or over time depending on the performance obligations in the contract. For performance obligations that are satisfied over time, such as services which require engineering and development based on customer requirements, the Company recognizes revenue using an input method based on contract costs incurred to date compared to total estimated contract costs.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 1pt;text-indent:36pt;">See Note <em style="font: inherit;">16,</em> Revenue, for additional information related to the application of ASC <em style="font: inherit;">606</em> to the Company&#8217;s primary revenue streams.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Sales taxes collected from customers and remitted to governmental authorities are accounted for on a net basis and therefore are excluded from revenues in the consolidated statements of operations and comprehensive loss.</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Arrangements with Multiple Performance Obligations</i></b></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">When a contract involves multiple performance obligations, the Company accounts for individual products and services separately if the customer can benefit from the product or service on its own or with other resources that are readily available to the customer and the product or service is separately identifiable from other promises in the arrangement. The consideration is allocated between separate performance obligations in proportion to their estimated standalone selling price (SSP). The SSP reflects the price the Company would charge for a specific product or service if it were sold separately in similar circumstances and to similar customers. If the selling price is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> directly observable, the Company determines SSP using information that <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>include other observable inputs, such as the cost plus margin approach, to estimate SSP. In instances where SSP is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> directly observable, the Company determines SSP using information that <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>include other observable inputs such as expected costs plus margin, or uses the residual approach for performance obligations whose SSP is highly variable or uncertain.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The Company provides standard product warranties for a term of typically <em style="font: inherit;"><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2025-12-31_RangeAxis-MinimumMember" name="us-gaap:ProductWarrantyObligationTerm" id="c142134362" format="ixt-sec:durday">90</ix:nonNumeric></em> days to <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142133805">one</span> year&#160;to ensure that its products comply with agreed-upon specifications. Standard warranties are considered to be assurance type warranties and are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> accounted for as separate performance obligations. Estimated future warranty costs are accrued and charged to cost of sales in the period that the related revenue is recognized. These estimates are based on historical warranty experience and any known or expected changes in warranty exposure, such as trends of product reliability and costs of repairing and replacing defective products. The Company assesses the adequacy of its recorded warranty liabilities on a quarterly basis and adjusts the amounts as necessary. Warranty costs are included within accrued expenses and other liabilities on the consolidated balance sheets. Refer to Note <em style="font: inherit;">8</em> for further information on warranty reserve amounts.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Other Policies, Judgments and Practical Expedients</i></b></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><i>Contract assets and liabilities. </i>Contract assets primarily represent revenues recognized for performance obligations that have been satisfied but for which amounts have <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> been billed. Contract liabilities relate to deferred revenue. Deferred revenue consists of amounts that have been invoiced and/or cash received but for which revenue has <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> been earned. This generally includes unrecognized revenue balances for development arrangements. Deferred revenue that will be realized during the succeeding <em style="font: inherit;">12</em>-month period is recorded within current liabilities and the remaining deferred revenue is recorded as noncurrent liabilities. The Company did <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142133811"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142134363">not</span></span> have any contract assets or contract liabilities&#160;as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 1pt;text-indent:36pt;"><i>Right of return. </i>The Company&#8217;s general terms and conditions for its contracts do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> contain a right of return that allows the customer to return products and receive a credit. Therefore, the Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> estimate returns and generally recognizes revenue at contract price upon product shipment or delivery.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><i>Significant financing component. </i>In certain arrangements, the Company receives payment from a customer either before or after the performance obligation has been satisfied. The expected timing difference between the payment and satisfaction of performance obligations for all of the Company&#8217;s contracts is <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> year or less&#894; therefore, the Company applies a practical expedient and does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> consider the effects of the time value of money on transaction price. The Company&#8217;s contracts with customer prepayment terms do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> include a significant financing component because the primary purpose is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> to receive financing from the customers. The Company did <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have any outstanding receivables with financing components as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><i>Contract modifications. </i>The Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>modify contracts to offer customers additional products or services. Each of the additional products and services are generally considered distinct from those products or services transferred to the customer before the modification. The Company evaluates whether the contract price for the additional products and services reflects the standalone selling price as adjusted for facts and circumstances applicable to that contract. In these cases, the Company accounts for the additional products or services as a separate contract. In other cases where the pricing in the modification does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> reflect the standalone selling price as adjusted for facts and circumstances applicable to that contract, the Company accounts for the additional products or services as part of the existing contract primarily on a prospective basis.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><i>Judgments and estimates. </i>Accounting for contracts recognized over time under ASC <em style="font: inherit;">606</em> involves the use of various techniques to estimate total contract revenue and costs. Due to uncertainties inherent in the estimation process, it is possible that estimates of costs to complete a contract will be revised in the near term. The Company reviews and updates its contract-related estimates quarterly, and records adjustments as needed. For those performance obligations for which revenue is recognized using a cost-to-cost input method, changes in total estimated costs, and related progress towards complete satisfaction of the performance obligation, are recognized in the period in which the revisions to the estimates are made.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b></b></p>
   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:CostOfSalesPolicyTextBlock" id="c142141381" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Cost of Revenue </b></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Cost of revenue primarily consists of costs directly associated with the production of lidar units&#160;that are held for sale and certain costs associated with development arrangements. Such costs for product&#160;are direct materials, direct labor, indirect labor, inventory write-downs, losses on purchase commitments, warranty expense, and allocation of overhead. Direct and indirect labor includes personnel-related costs and packaging and procurement respectively associated with the production of lidar units. Other costs such as indirect manufacturing costs are recognized in research and development and general and administrative expenses on the consolidated statements of operations and comprehensive loss. Costs associated with development arrangements include the direct costs and allocation of overhead costs involved in the execution of the contract.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric>

   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:ResearchAndDevelopmentExpensePolicy" id="c142141382" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Research and Development Expenses</b></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Research and development expenses include personnel costs (including salaries, benefits, bonuses,&#160;and stock-based compensation), new hardware and software materials to the extent <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> future economic benefits are expected, other related expenses such as lab equipment, <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> party development-related contractors, and allocated overhead expenses. Substantially all the R&amp;D expenses are related to the development of new products and services, including contract development expenses. They are expensed as incurred and included in the consolidated statements of operation and comprehensive loss.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b></b></p>
   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationOptionAndIncentivePlansPolicy" id="c142141383" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Stock-Based Compensation</b></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The Company accounts for stock-based compensation by measuring and recognizing compensation expense for all share-based awards based on estimated grant-date fair values. The Company uses the straight-line attribution method to allocate compensation cost to reporting periods over each awardee&#8217;s requisite service period, which is generally the vesting period of the award. The Company measures nonemployee awards at the date of grant, which generally is the date at which a grantor and a grantee reach a mutual understanding of the key terms and conditions of a share-based payment award. The Company&#8217;s policy is to recognize the effect of forfeitures in the period they occur. The grant-date fair value of the restricted stock units, or &#8220;RSUs,&#8221; is equal to the fair market value of the Company&#8217;s common stock on the grant date. The grant-date fair value for stock options and stock purchase rights under the employee stock purchase plan ("ESPP") is estimated using the Black-Scholes option-pricing model. The grant-date fair value for RSUs with an associated market condition is estimated using the Monte-Carlo simulation model. Both the Black-Scholes option-pricing model and the Monte-Carlo simulation model require the input of subjective assumptions, including the award&#8217;s expected term and the price volatility of the underlying stock.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b></b></p>
   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxPolicyTextBlock" id="c142141384" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Income Taxes</b></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Income taxes are accounted for under the asset and liability method. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are recognized for the future tax consequences attributable to differences between the financial statements carrying amounts of existing assets and liabilities and their respective tax bases, as well as net operating loss and tax credit carryforwards. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured using enacted tax rates expected to apply to taxable income in the years in which those temporary differences are expected to be recovered or settled. The effect on deferred tax assets and liabilities of a change in tax rates is recognized in income in the period that includes the enactment date.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The Company recognizes deferred tax assets to the extent that these assets are more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> to be realized. In making such a determination, the Company considers all available positive and negative evidence, including future reversals of existing taxable temporary differences, projected future taxable income, tax-planning strategies, and results of recent operations. If the Company determines that it would be able to realize deferred tax assets in the future in excess of their net recorded amount, an adjustment to the deferred tax asset valuation allowance would be made to reduce the provision for income taxes.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The Company records uncertain tax positions in accordance with FASB ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">740,</em> <i>Income Taxes</i> (&#8220;ASC <em style="font: inherit;">740&#8221;</em>) on the basis of a <em style="font: inherit;">two</em>-step process in which determinations are made (<em style="font: inherit;">1</em>)&#160;whether it is more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> that the tax positions will be sustained on the basis of the technical merits of the position and (<em style="font: inherit;">2</em>)&#160;for those tax positions that meet the more-likely-than-<em style="font: inherit;">not</em> recognition threshold, the Company recognizes the largest amount of tax benefit that is more than <em style="font: inherit;">50%</em> likely to be realized upon ultimate settlement with the related tax authority.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The Company recognizes interest and penalties related to unrecognized tax benefits in the provision for income tax expense in the accompanying consolidated statements of operations and comprehensive loss. Accrued interest and penalties are included in accrued expenses and other current liabilities in the consolidated balance sheets. As of and for the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, there were <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142133834"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142134364">no</span></span> interest or penalties recorded.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b></b></p>
   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:EarningsPerSharePolicyTextBlock" id="c142141385" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Net Loss per Share</b></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Basic net loss per share is computed using net loss available to common stockholders divided by the weighted average number of common shares outstanding during the period. Diluted net loss per share reflects the dilutive effects of stock options, restricted stock units, preferred stock, stock to be issued under the ESPP, convertible notes, and warrants outstanding during the period to the extent such securities would <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be anti-dilutive and is determined using the if-converted and treasury stock methods.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The Company calculates weighted average number of common shares outstanding during the period using the Company&#8217;s common stock outstanding.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Basic and diluted net loss per share attributable to common stockholders was the same for all periods presented as the inclusion of all potentially dilutive securities outstanding was anti-dilutive, as AEye is currently operating in a net loss position.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>

   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:ComprehensiveIncomePolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c142141386" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Comprehensive Income (Loss)</b></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Comprehensive income (loss) includes all changes in equity (net assets) from non-owner sources during a period and net unrealized gains (losses) on available-for-sale debt securities.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric>

   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c142141387" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Recent Accounting Pronouncements</b></p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2024, </em>the FASB issued ASU&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03,</em> <i>Disaggregation of Income Statement Expenses</i>, which requires annual and interim disclosure of disaggregated disclosures of certain costs and expenses on the income statement. The standard is effective for fiscal years beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2026, </em>and interim periods within fiscal years beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2027, </em>with early adoption permitted. Amendments are applied on a prospective basis with retrospective application permitted. The Company is currently evaluating the impact of this guidance.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:FairValueDisclosuresTextBlock" id="c3138580" escape="true">
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 36pt;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">2.</em></b></p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>FAIR VALUE MEASUREMENTS</b></p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The fair value of the Company&#8217;s financial assets and liabilities is determined in accordance with the fair value hierarchy established in FASB ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">820,</em> <i>Fair Value Measurements and Disclosures</i> (&#8220;ASC <em style="font: inherit;">820&#8221;</em>). ASC&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">820</em> defines fair value as the exchange price that would be received for an asset or paid to transfer a liability (an exit price) in the principal or most advantageous market for the asset or liability in an orderly transaction between market participants on the measurement date. The fair value hierarchy of ASC&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">820</em> requires an entity to maximize the use of observable inputs when measuring fair value and classifies those inputs into <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> levels:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Level</i></b>&#160;<b><i><em style="font: inherit;">1</em></i></b>&#8212;Observable inputs, such as quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Level</i></b>&#160;<b><i><em style="font: inherit;">2</em></i></b>&#8212;Observable inputs, other than Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> inputs, which are observable either directly or indirectly or can be corroborated by observable market data using quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Level</i></b>&#160;<b><i><em style="font: inherit;">3</em></i></b>&#8212;Unobservable inputs in which there is little or <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> market data, which require the reporting entity to develop its own assumptions.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 1pt;text-indent:36pt;">The Company's financial instruments that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> remeasured at fair value include accounts receivable, prepaid and other current assets, accounts payable, accrued expenses, other current and noncurrent liabilities, and the noncurrent convertible note. The carrying values of these financial instruments approximate their fair values.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The Company&#8217;s financial assets and liabilities measured at fair value on a recurring basis and the level of inputs used for such measurements were as follows (in thousands):</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The Company&#8217;s financial assets and liabilities subject to fair value procedures were comprised of the following:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 1pt;text-indent:36pt;"><i>Money Market Funds: </i>The Company holds financial assets consisting of money market funds. These securities are valued using observable inputs, such as quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><i>Marketable Securities</i>: The Company holds financial assets consisting of fixed-income U.S. government securities, corporate bonds,&#160;commercial paper, agency bonds, and asset-backed securities. The securities are valued using prices from independent pricing services based on quoted prices of identical instruments in less active or inactive markets. Additionally, quoted prices of similar instruments in active market or industry models using data inputs such as interest rates and prices that can be directly observed or corroborated in active markets are used to value marketable securities.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><i>Derivative Warrant Liability</i>: On <em style="font: inherit;"> September 15, 2022, </em>the Company entered into a convertible note agreement with a face value of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142133857" contextRef="i_2022-09-15_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2022NoteMember_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-ConvertibleDebtMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">10,500</ix:nonFraction> (the <em style="font: inherit;">"2022</em> Note"). The Company issued&#160;warrants&#160;as part of the <em style="font: inherit;">2022</em> Note. The warrants are recorded on the consolidated balance sheets at fair value. The fair value is based on unobservable inputs, which represent Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> measurements within the fair value hierarchy. The fair value estimate of the warrants was based on a Monte-Carlo simulation model. Inherent in a Monte-Carlo simulation model are assumptions related to price, volatility, risk-free interest rate, term to expiration, and dividend yield. The price is based on the publicly traded price of the Company's common stock as of the measurement date. The Company estimated the volatility for the warrants based on the historical and implied volatilities of the Company's publicly traded common stock. The risk-free interest rate is based on interpolated U.S. Treasury rates, commensurate with a similar term to the warrants. The term to expiration was calculated as the contractual term of the warrants of <em style="font: inherit;">five</em> years. Finally, the Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> currently anticipate paying a dividend. Any changes in these assumptions can change the valuation significantly. Changes in fair value are recognized in other income (expense) for each reporting period. Derivative Warrant Liability was included within other noncurrent liabilities on the consolidated balance sheets. These warrants were cancelled on <em style="font: inherit;"> July 28, 2025.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> January&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">2025,</em> the Company entered into a convertible note agreement with a face value of&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c142133864" contextRef="i_2025-01-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2025NoteMember_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-ConvertibleDebtMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">3,000</ix:nonFraction>&#160;(the <em style="font: inherit;">"2025</em> Note"). The Company issued a warrant&#160;to purchase up to&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c142133866" contextRef="i_2025-01-31_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-The2025NoteWarrantsMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightNumberOfSecuritiesCalledByWarrantsOrRights" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">805,263</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock. The warrant was recorded on the accompanying consolidated balance sheet at fair value. The fair value is based on unobservable inputs, which represent Level&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">3</em>&#160;measurements within the fair value hierarchy. The fair value estimate of the warrant&#160;was based on a Black-Scholes&#160;model. Inherent in a Black-Scholes model are assumptions related to price, volatility, risk-free interest rate, term to expiration, and dividend yield.&#160;Changes in fair value were recognized in other income (expense) for each reporting period. Derivative Warrant Liability was included within other noncurrent liabilities on the consolidated balance sheets. These warrants were exercised in full on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> July 28, 2025</em><i>.</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">In&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> August&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">2025</em><i>,</i>&#160;in connection with the lease settlement (see Note <em style="font: inherit;">5</em>&#160;for details of the settlement), the Company issued&#160;warrants, which are&#160;recorded on the accompanying consolidated balance sheets at fair value. The fair value is based on unobservable inputs, which represent Level&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">3</em>&#160;measurements within the fair value hierarchy. The fair value estimate of the warrants was based on a Black-Scholes&#160;model. Inherent in a Black-Scholes model are assumptions related to price, volatility, risk-free interest rate, term to expiration, and dividend yield.&#160;Changes in fair value are recognized in other income (expense) for each reporting period. Derivative Warrant Liability is included within other noncurrent liabilities on the consolidated balance sheets.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><i>Private Placement Warrant Liability</i>: The Private Placement Warrants are recorded on the consolidated balance sheets at fair value. The fair value is based on observable Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> inputs, specifically, the observable input of the Company's public warrants, as terms of both warrants are substantially similar. Any changes in the fair value of the liability are reflected in other income (expense), net, on the consolidated statements of operations and comprehensive loss. Private Placement Warrant liability is included within other noncurrent liabilities on the consolidated balance sheets.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 45pt;">If factors or assumptions change, the estimated fair values could be materially different. The value of the Company&#8217;s derivative warrant liabilities would increase if a higher risk-free interest rate was used&#160;and would decrease if a lower risk-free interest rate was used. Similarly, a higher volatility assumption would increase the value of the liabilities, and a lower volatility assumption would decrease the value of the liabilities.</p>

   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 36pt;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">5.</em></b></p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>LEASES</b></p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The Company leases office facilities in Northern California under non-cancelable operating leases. In <em style="font: inherit;"> July 2024, </em>the Company entered into <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142133887">two</span> new long-term leases, <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142133888">one</span> of which the Company uses as its headquarters, which was amended in <em style="font: inherit;"> February 2026 </em>to extend the term and add additional square footage.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Some of the Company's leases include options to renew, with renewal terms that, if exercised by the Company, extend the lease term&#160;for <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142133889">five</span> years. The exercise of these renewal options is at the Company's discretion. The Company's lease agreements do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> contain any material terms and conditions of residual value guarantees or material restrictive covenants. The Company's short-term lease expense was determined to <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be material.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> November 14, 2023, </em>the Company assigned an operating lease resulting in the Company being relieved of its primary obligation under this lease. As a result of the lease assignment, a new tenant assumed the primary obligation under the lease, with the Company becoming secondarily liable. If the new tenant should fail to perform under the lease, the Company could be liable to fulfill any remaining lease obligations. The lease had a remaining term of <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseRemainingLeaseTerm" id="c142133892" format="ixt-sec:duryear">1.7</ix:nonNumeric> years as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025&#160;</em>with the Company serving as guarantor for the remaining term. The resulting maximum exposure includes $<ix:nonFraction id="c142133893" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_PropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis-OfficeFacilitiesInNorthernCaliforniaMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseLiabilityPaymentsDue" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">166</ix:nonFraction> of undiscounted future minimum lease payments plus potential additional payments to satisfy maintenance, taxes, and insurance requirements for the remainder of the lease term.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> August 2024,&#160;</em><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142133894">one</span>&#160;of the Company's existing leases, originally set to expire on <em style="font: inherit;"> November 30, 2026, </em>was terminated early.&#160;In conjunction with the early termination, the Company recorded a net gain of&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c142133895" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="lidr:GainLossOnTerminationOfLeaseNet" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">491</ix:nonFraction>&#160;on termination of the operating lease during the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024. </em>The net gain&#160;included&#160;a gain of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142133896" contextRef="d_2024-08-01_2024-08-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:GainLossOnTerminationOfLease" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">5,954</ix:nonFraction>, comprised of a $<ix:nonFraction id="c142133897" contextRef="d_2024-08-01_2024-08-31" unitRef="USD" name="lidr:TerminationOfLeaseReductionOfLiability" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">16,325</ix:nonFraction> net liability reduction, partially offset by a $<ix:nonFraction id="c142133898" contextRef="d_2024-08-01_2024-08-31" unitRef="USD" name="lidr:TerminationOfLeaseReductionOfRightofuseAsset" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">10,371</ix:nonFraction> decrease in its remaining right of use asset.&#160; Additionally, in accordance with&#160;terms in the lease agreement and based on certain assumptions, the Company&#160;recorded a lease termination loss&#160;of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142133899" contextRef="i_2024-08-31" unitRef="USD" name="lidr:LeaseTerminationLiability" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">5,463</ix:nonFraction>,&#160;representing&#160;estimated unpaid rent for the remaining term.&#160;The net gain was&#160;recorded&#160;in general and administrative expenses in the consolidated statement of&#160;operations and comprehensive loss.&#160;The lease termination liability was reduced by the draw-down of the $<ix:nonFraction id="c142133900" contextRef="d_2024-08-01_2024-08-31" unitRef="USD" name="lidr:LeaseTerminationLiabilityReductionFromDrawdownOfCollateral" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">2,150</ix:nonFraction> letter of credit by the landlord in <em style="font: inherit;"> August 2024;&#160;</em>the remaining lease termination liability of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142133901" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="lidr:LeaseTerminationLiability" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">3,313</ix:nonFraction> as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024</em>&#160;was&#160;recorded in accrued expenses and other current liabilities in the&#160;consolidated balance sheet.&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">2025</em></b>&#160;<b>Convertible Note</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">In&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> January&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">2025,</em>&#160;the Company entered into a Securities Purchase Agreement with a certain institutional investor and issued (i) a senior&#160;unsecured convertible promissory note (the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">"2025</em>&#160;Note")&#160;for an aggregate principal amount of&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c142133934" contextRef="i_2025-01-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2025NoteMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">3,240</ix:nonFraction>&#160;for an aggregate purchase&#160;price of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142133935" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-01-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2025NoteMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromConvertibleDebt" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">3,000</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and (ii) a&#160;warrant&#160;to purchase up to&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c142133936" contextRef="i_2025-01-31_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-The2025NoteWarrantsMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightNumberOfSecuritiesCalledByWarrantsOrRights" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">805,263</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock.    <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Monthly redemptions began in&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> April 2025&#160;</em>and were&#160;due on the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">first</em>&#160;of each subsequent month (each a "Monthly Redemption Date" or an "Installment Date").&#160;The Company was required to redeem the Monthly Redemption Amount until the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;Note was fully redeemed, paid&#160;in cash or, so long as certain equity conditions are met, shares of our common stock. If the Company elects to settle such redemptions in shares of common stock, the number of shares to be settled shall be based on an Installment Conversion Price equal to the lower of (i) $<ix:nonFraction id="c142133955" contextRef="i_2025-01-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2025NoteMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentConvertibleConversionPrice1" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">2.22</ix:nonFraction>&#160;or (ii) the greater of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142133956" contextRef="i_2025-01-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2025NoteMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="lidr:DebtInstrumentConvertibleConversionPriceUsedInCalculation" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">0.30</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c142133957" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-01-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2025NoteMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentConvertibleThresholdPercentageOfStockPriceTrigger" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">90</ix:nonFraction>% of average&#160;volume weighted average&#160;price of the common stock during the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">five</em>&#160;(<em style="font: inherit;">5</em>) trading days immediately preceding&#160;the applicable Monthly Redemption Date.&#160;The investor is permitted,&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;exceeding&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">five</em>&#160;times, to accelerate up to&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">one</em>&#160;Monthly&#160;Installment Amount,&#160;between Installments, (each, an "Acceleration," and each such amount, an "Acceleration Amount", and the Conversion Date of any such&#160;Acceleration, each an "Acceleration Date") at the Acceleration Conversion Price. The Acceleration Conversion Price shall be the lower of (i) $<ix:nonFraction id="c142133963" contextRef="i_2025-01-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2025NoteMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentConvertibleConversionPrice1" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">2.22</ix:nonFraction>&#160;or (ii) the greater of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142133964" contextRef="i_2025-01-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2025NoteMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="lidr:DebtInstrumentConvertibleConversionPriceUsedInCalculation" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">0.30</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c142133965" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-01-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2025NoteMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentConvertibleThresholdPercentageOfStockPriceTrigger" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">90</ix:nonFraction>% of average&#160;volume weighted average price of the common stock during the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">five</em>&#160;(<ix:nonFraction id="c142133967" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-01-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2025NoteMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentConvertibleThresholdConsecutiveTradingDays1" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">5</ix:nonFraction>) trading days immediately preceding&#160;the applicable Acceleration Date.&#160;&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;Note&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> may&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;be converted into common stock to the extent such conversion would result in the investor and its affiliates having beneficial ownership of more than&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c142133970" contextRef="i_2025-01-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2025NoteMember" unitRef="Pure" name="lidr:DebtInstrumentConvertibleMaximumBeneficialOwnershipPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">19.99</ix:nonFraction>% of our then outstanding shares of common stock.    <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company and investor entered into a registration rights agreement (the &#8220;Registration Rights Agreement&#8221;) to which the Company was required to file a registration statement registering the resale by the investor&#160;of any shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock issuable upon conversion, including the resale of shares issuable upon exercise of the associated warrants. The Company is required to meet certain obligations with respect to the timeliness of the filing and effectiveness of the registration statement. The Company filed such registration statement on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> January 16, 2025,&#160;</em>and an amendment thereto on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> February 25, 2025,&#160;</em>which was declared effective by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March 4, 2025.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company elected to apply the fair value option to the measurement of the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;Note. As a result of adopting the fair value option,&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">no</em>&#160;embedded derivatives are bifurcated from the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;Note. The Company classified&#160;the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;Note as a liability at fair value and remeasured the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;Note to fair value at each reporting period. The total proceeds received from the investor of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142133976" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-01-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2025NoteMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromConvertibleDebt" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">3,000</ix:nonFraction> was allocated between the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;Note and the related warrants issued using the relative fair value method at issuance date. This resulted in an initial fair value of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142133978" contextRef="i_2025-01-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2025NoteMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ConvertibleDebtFairValueDisclosures" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">3,266</ix:nonFraction>&#160;being allocated to the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;Note, and $<ix:nonFraction id="c142133980" contextRef="i_2025-01-31_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-The2025NoteWarrantsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:WarrantsAndRightsOutstanding" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">1,046</ix:nonFraction>&#160;allocated to the associated warrants. The Company recorded&#160;a non-cash issuance cost&#160;of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142133981" contextRef="i_2025-01-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2025NoteMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredFinanceCostsNet" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">1,312</ix:nonFraction>, representing the difference between the fair value and proceeds received, within Interest expense and other on the consolidated statement of operations. The fair value measurement included&#160;the assumption of accrued interest and expense and thus a separate amount was&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;reflected on the consolidated statement of operations.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">During the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025,&#160;</em>the Company made cash payments of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142133983" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2025NoteMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RepaymentsOfDebt" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">989</ix:nonFraction>. Additionally, $<ix:nonFraction id="c142133984" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_DebtConversionByUniqueDescriptionAxis-ConversionOfThe2025NoteIntoCommonStockMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtConversionOriginalDebtAmount1" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">2,591</ix:nonFraction>&#160;in aggregate principal and interest were converted into&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c142133985" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_DebtConversionByUniqueDescriptionAxis-ConversionOfThe2025NoteIntoCommonStockMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:DebtConversionConvertedInstrumentSharesIssued1" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">2,405,573</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares of&#160;common stock. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em>the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;Note was fully repaid and all associated warrants fully exercised.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b>Class A Common Stock </b>&#8212;<b> </b>Class A common stock has the following rights:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Voting rights:</span> Each holder of Class A common stock will be entitled to <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> (<ix:nonFraction id="c142133995" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="lidr:CommonStockVotingRightsNumberOfVotes" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1</ix:nonFraction>) vote in person or by proxy for each share of the Class A common stock held of record by such holder. The holders of shares of the Class A common stock will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have cumulative voting rights. Except as otherwise required in the Charter or by applicable law, the holders of the Class A common stock vote together as a single class on all matters on which stockholders are generally entitled to vote.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Dividend rights:</span> Subject to any other provisions of the Charter, each holder of Class A common stock will be entitled to receive, in proportion to the number of shares of the Class A common stock held, such dividends and other distributions in cash, stock, or property of the Company when, as and if declared thereon by the Board from time to time out of assets or funds of the Company legally available therefor.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Rights upon liquidation:</span> In the event of any liquidation, dissolution, or winding up (either voluntary or involuntary) of the Company, after payments to creditors of the Company that <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>at the time be outstanding, and subject to the rights of any holders of the Company preferred stock that <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>then be outstanding, holders of shares of the Class A common stock will be entitled to receive ratably, in proportion to the number of shares of the Class A common stock held by them, all remaining assets of the Company available for distribution.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b>Preferred Stock </b>&#8212; The Company has the authority, without stockholder approval, to issue shares of preferred stock from time to time on terms it <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>determine, to divide shares of preferred stock into <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> or more class or series and to fix for each such class or series the designations, preferences, privileges, and restrictions of preferred stock, including dividend rights, conversion rights, voting rights, terms of redemption, liquidation preference, and the number of shares constituting any series or the designation of any series to the fullest extent permitted by the Delaware General Corporation Law. The issuance of the Company&#8217;s preferred stock could have the effect of decreasing the trading price of the Class A common stock, restricting dividends on the capital stock of the Company, diluting the voting power of the Class A common stock, impairing the liquidation rights of the capital stock of the Company, or delaying or preventing a change in control of the Company. Although the Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> currently intend to issue any shares of preferred stock, the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>choose to do so in the future.</p>

   <div style="font-size: 10pt; text-indent: 36pt;">
     In connection with the CSPA, the Company issued to New Circle&#160;
    <ix:nonFraction id="c142134054" contextRef="d_2024-07-25_2024-07-25_CounterpartyNameAxis-NewCirclePrincipalInvestmentsLLCMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-SharePurchaseAgreementMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">225,563</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares of common stock in the Company as commitment shares for the facility. At issuance, the
    <ix:nonFraction id="c142134055" contextRef="d_2024-07-25_2024-07-25_CounterpartyNameAxis-NewCirclePrincipalInvestmentsLLCMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-SharePurchaseAgreementMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">225,563</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares of common stock had a fair value of&#160;
    $<ix:nonFraction id="c142134056" contextRef="d_2024-07-25_2024-07-25_CounterpartyNameAxis-NewCirclePrincipalInvestmentsLLCMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-SharePurchaseAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodValueNewIssues" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">282</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and were recorded to Interest expense and other in the Company's consolidated statement of operations and comprehensive loss. The Company determined that the right to sell additional shares represents a freestanding put option under ASC
    <em style="font: inherit;">815,</em>&#160;
    <i style="font-size: 10pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Derivatives and Hedging</i>, and as such, the financial instrument was classified as a derivative asset with a fair value of
    <em style="font: inherit;">zero</em> at inception of the CSPA on
    <em style="font: inherit;"> July 25, 2024.</em>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 1pt;text-indent:36pt;">This CSPA agreement was terminated in <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2025. </em>In total, the Company issued&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c142134059" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_CounterpartyNameAxis-NewCirclePrincipalInvestmentsLLCMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-SharePurchaseAgreementMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">8,980,713</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares of its common stock, including commitment&#160;shares, for&#160;gross proceeds totaling $<ix:nonFraction id="c142134060" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_CounterpartyNameAxis-NewCirclePrincipalInvestmentsLLCMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-SharePurchaseAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodValueNewIssues" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">27,754</ix:nonFraction>.&#160;<i>&#65279;</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><b>Alliance Global Partners (&#8220;A.G.P.&#8221;) At Market Issuance Sales Agreement (the &#8220;ATM Agreement&#8221;)</b> &#8212; On <em style="font: inherit;"> September 12, 2024, </em>the Company entered into the ATM and a Registration Rights Agreement with A.G.P. Under the terms and subject to the conditions of the ATM Agreement, the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>issue and sell through A.G.P. the Company's common stock having an aggregate value offering price of up to $<ix:nonFraction id="c142134061" contextRef="i_2024-09-12_CounterpartyNameAxis-AllianceGlobalPartnersAgpMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-AtMarketIssuanceSalesAgreementTheAtmMember" unitRef="USD" name="lidr:EquityOfferingMaximumAmount" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2,600</ix:nonFraction> ("Placement Shares") from time to time through an "at-the-market" equity offering program. The Company has sole discretion to initiate such sales of common stock over a period of <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-09-12_2024-09-12_CounterpartyNameAxis-AllianceGlobalPartnersAgpMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-AtMarketIssuanceSalesAgreementTheAtmMember" name="lidr:EquityOfferingPeriod" id="c142134062" format="ixt-sec:durmonth">36</ix:nonNumeric> months. Under the terms and subject to the conditions of the ATM Agreement, the Company will set the parameters for the sale of shares, including the number or dollar amount of Placement Shares to be issued, the time period during which sales are requested to be made, any limitation on the number or dollar amount of Placement Shares that <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be sold in any <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> trading day and any minimum price below which sales <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em><em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be made. In <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2025, </em>the Company increased the aggregate amount available under the ATM program to $<ix:nonFraction id="c142134066" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_CounterpartyNameAxis-AllianceGlobalPartnersAgpMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-AtMarketIssuanceSalesAgreementTheAtmMember" unitRef="USD" name="lidr:EquityOfferingMaximumAmount" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">125,000</ix:nonFraction>, following multiple prior increases since the original agreement.</p>

   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 36pt;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">14.</em></b></p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>STOCK-BASED COMPENSATION</b></p> </td></tr>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The Company has <em style="font: inherit;">six</em>&#160;equity incentive plans, the <em style="font: inherit;">2014</em> US LADAR Inc. Equity Incentive Plan (the <em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;2014</em> Plan&#8221;), the <em style="font: inherit;">2016</em> Stock Plan (the <em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;2016</em> Plan&#8221;), the <em style="font: inherit;">2021</em> Equity Incentive Plan (the &#8220;Incentive Plan&#8221;), the <em style="font: inherit;">2022</em> Employee Stock Purchase Plan (the "ESPP"),&#160; the <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em> CEO Inducement Grant Plan (the "CEO Plan"),&#160;and the <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> Employment Inducement Incentive Award Plan, (<em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;2025</em> EIIAP&#8221;). On <em style="font: inherit;"> August&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">16,</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2021,</em> the Company&#8217;s <em style="font: inherit;">2014</em> Plan and <em style="font: inherit;">2016</em> Plan were terminated in connection with the closing of the business combination as defined in Note <em style="font: inherit;">1,</em> but continue to govern the terms of outstanding equity awards that were granted prior to the termination of the plans.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; "><em style="font: inherit;">2014</em> Plan and <em style="font: inherit;">2016</em> Plan</span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The <em style="font: inherit;">2014</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2016</em> Plan provide for the grant of incentive stock options to employees only and non-statutory stock options and RSUs to employees, directors, and consultants of the Company. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> August&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">16,</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2021,</em> the Company <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> longer grants equity awards pursuant to the <em style="font: inherit;">2014</em> Plan or <em style="font: inherit;">2016</em> Plan, and as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, <ix:nonFraction id="c142134104" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_PlanNameAxis-The2014And2016EquityIncentivePlansMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsGrantsInPeriod" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">58,056</ix:nonFraction>&#160;RSUs were granted.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Under the <em style="font: inherit;">2016</em>&#160;Plan, options to purchase common stock generally vest over <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142134106">four</span> years with <ix:nonFraction id="c142134107" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_PlanNameAxis-The2016PlanMember_VestingAxis-ShareBasedCompensationAwardTrancheOneMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingRightsPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">25</ix:nonFraction>% vesting at the end of the <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> year and the rest vesting ratably over the next <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142134109">three</span> years. RSUs generally vest <ix:nonFraction id="c142134110" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_PlanNameAxis-The2016PlanMember_VestingAxis-ShareBasedCompensationAwardTrancheTwoMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingRightsPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">25</ix:nonFraction>% at the end of the <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> year with the remaining RSUs vesting ratably over the next <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> years or they vest ratably over the <em style="font: inherit;">four</em> years. Under the <em style="font: inherit;">2014</em>&#160;Plan, the vesting period for options to purchase common stock range from immediate to <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142134115">four</span> years. Under each plan, the options expire <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142134116">ten</span> years from the date of grant.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 1pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; "><em style="font: inherit;">2021</em> Equity Incentive Plan</span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The Incentive Plan became effective immediately upon the closing of the business combination on <em style="font: inherit;"> August&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">16,</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2021</em> and initially reserved <ix:nonFraction id="c142134120" contextRef="i_2021-08-16_PlanNameAxis-The2021PlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:CommonStockCapitalSharesReservedForFutureIssuance" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">514,681</ix:nonFraction> shares of common stock for issuance thereunder. The Incentive Plan includes an evergreen provision that provides for an annual increase in the number of shares of common stock available for issuance thereunder beginning on <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2022 </em>and ending on <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2032, </em>equal to <ix:nonFraction id="c142134121" contextRef="d_2021-08-16_2021-08-16_PlanNameAxis-The2021PlanMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardPercentageOfOutstandingStockMaximum" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">5</ix:nonFraction>% of the shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock outstanding on <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2021 </em>for the <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> year and by <ix:nonFraction id="c142134123" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_PlanNameAxis-The2021PlanMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardPercentageOfOutstandingStockMaximum" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">3</ix:nonFraction>% of the total number of shares of common stock outstanding on <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31 </em>of the preceding calendar year for each year thereafter, or a lesser number of shares as determined by the Board of Directors. Since <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2022, </em>the Board of Directors have authorized the addition of <ix:nonFraction id="c142134124" contextRef="d_2022-01-01_2022-01-01_PlanNameAxis-The2021PlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfAdditionalSharesAuthorized" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,549,868</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares of common stock to be added to the Incentive Plan for issuance.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Under the Incentive Plan, RSU&#8217;s vest depending on their vesting schedule. For newly hired employees, RSU&#8217;s generally vest <ix:nonFraction id="c142134125" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_GranteeStatusAxis-SharebasedPaymentArrangementNewEmployeeMember_PlanNameAxis-The2021PlanMember_VestingAxis-ShareBasedCompensationAwardTrancheOneMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingRightsPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">25</ix:nonFraction>% during the quarterly release date following the recipient&#8217;s <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142134126">one</span> year anniversary of their start date. The remaining amounts generally vest quarterly over the next <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142134127">two</span>&#160;years. For existing employees, these RSUs generally vest quarterly over <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142134128">one</span> year. The fair value of the RSU is equal to the fair value of the Company&#8217;s common stock on the date of grant.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The Company adds back cancelled, unvested&#160;shares&#160;and those shares withheld in connection with the net share settlement of vested RSU's to the pool of shares available for&#160;future grants. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, <ix:nonFraction id="c142134129" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_PlanNameAxis-The2021PlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsGrantsInPeriod" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">3,225,045</ix:nonFraction>&#160;RSUs were granted to certain individuals under the Incentive Plan.</p>
